doc.name: A — pet accessories catalogue, mirror tunnel, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: waxed-canvas dog collar
Category: pet accessories
Shot programme: mirror tunnel
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You run the tabletop stage for a premium pet accessories product shoot. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the macro detail insert in a mirror tunnel treatment.

SUBJECT. A waxed-canvas dog collar. The reference image governs silhouette, material finish and every printed mark. Reproduce the label text exactly as it appears; never invent new copy, logos or claims.

CAMERA. Extreme macro on the closure, seam, texture or applicator — product only partly in frame. Shoot on a 70-200mm zoom at 150mm at f/11, framing for a stacked layered composition with three depth planes.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with tungsten practicals in frame carrying the warm layer. Stage the product on or against frosted glass, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a sun-bleached grade with faded blacks and a green-yellow bias. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Reply with a single continuous prompt paragraph. Never explain, never bullet, never wrap it in markdown fences.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
